symbols.name: P-certified
symbols.def: \(P_t\subseteq\operatorname{pa}_{\cup}(t)\) is the certified-parent set maintained for head \(t\) by the cycle-free policy

symbols.name: anc-relation
symbols.def: \(a\,R_{\mathbf G}\,b\) iff \(a\) is an ancestor of \(b\) in at least one \(\mathcal G_\ell\)

symbols.name: ancestor-graph
symbols.def: \(\mathcal C_{\mathbf G}(t)\) is \(R_{\mathbf G}\) restricted to \(\{a\in V:aR_{\mathbf G}t\}\)

symbols.name: kappa-ell-i
symbols.role: observational causal mechanism of vertex \(i\) in component \(\ell\)

symbols.name: kappa-lift
symbols.def: \(\widetilde\kappa_{\ell i}(dx_i\mid x_{\operatorname{pa}_{\cup}(i)})=\kappa_{\ell i}(dx_i\mid x_{\operatorname{pa}_{\ell}(i)})\), with coordinates outside \(\operatorname{pa}_{\ell}(i)\) ignored

symbols.name: P-ell
symbols.role: component law induced by the observational DAG factorization

symbols.name: q-i
symbols.def: \(q_i(dx_i)\) is indexed only by \(i\), hence is shared across components and across every target containing \(i\)

symbols.name: Delta
symbols.role: exact mechanism-variation set after lifting mechanisms to the union-parent domain

symbols.name: y
symbols.role: single latent root of the I-mixture DAG

symbols.name: G-mix-I
symbols.def: \(\mathcal G_{\mathrm m,I}=((V\times L)\cup\{y\},\,\bigcup_{\ell\in L}\{((u,\ell),(v,\ell)):(u,v)\in E(\mathcal G_{\ell,I})\}\cup\{(y,(i,\ell)):i\in\Delta\setminus I,\ \ell\in L\})\)

symbols.name: O-G
symbols.role: all conditional-independence answers under \(P_I\), equivalently all barred-copy d-separations by simultaneous I-mixture faithfulness

symbols.name: algorithm-A
symbols.role: chooses paid targets from past oracle answers

symbols.name: G-alt
symbols.type: finite family of legal alternative models

assumptions.condition: \(\mathcal G_\ell=(V,E_\ell)\) is a directed acyclic graph for every \(\ell\in L\).
For every \(I\subseteq V\) and every pairwise disjoint \(A,B,C\subseteq V\), \(X_A\perp_{P_I}X_B\mid X_C\) if and only if \(\overline A\perp_{d,\mathcal G_{\mathrm m,I}}\overline B\mid\overline C\).
\(\operatorname{skel}(\mathcal G_\ell)\) is a tree for every \(\ell\in L\).

definitions.name: component observational laws
definitions.construction: For every \(\ell\in L\), \(P_\ell(dx_V)=\prod_{i\in V}\kappa_{\ell i}(dx_i\mid x_{\operatorname{pa}_\ell(i)})\), where the product is evaluated in any topological order of \(\mathcal G_\ell\).

definitions.name: \(\Delta(\mathbf G,\boldsymbol\kappa)\)
definitions.construction: \(\Delta(\mathbf G,\boldsymbol\kappa)=\{i\in V:\exists\ell,\ell'\in L,\ \widetilde\kappa_{\ell i}(\cdot\mid x_{\operatorname{pa}_{\cup}(i)})\not\equiv\widetilde\kappa_{\ell' i}(\cdot\mid x_{\operatorname{pa}_{\cup}(i)})\}\), where every component mechanism is lifted to the common union-parent argument by ignoring coordinates outside its component-parent set.

definitions.name: shared stochastic hard intervention
definitions.construction: For every \(I\subseteq V\) and \(\ell\in L\), \(\mathcal G_{\ell,I}=(V,\{(u,v)\in E(\mathcal G_\ell):v\notin I\})\) and \(P_{\ell,I}(dx_V)=\prod_{i\in I}q_i(dx_i)\prod_{i\in V\setminus I}\kappa_{\ell i}(dx_i\mid x_{\operatorname{pa}_\ell(i)})\); the same \(q_i\) is used in every component and every intervention containing \(i\).

definitions.name: \(P_I\)
definitions.construction: \(P_I=\sum_{\ell\in L}w_\ell P_{\ell,I}\) for every \(I\subseteq V\), with \(P_{\varnothing}=\sum_{\ell\in L}w_\ell P_\ell\).

definitions.name: \(\mathcal G_{\mathrm m,I}\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal G_{\mathrm m,I}=((V\times L)\cup\{y\},\,\bigcup_{\ell\in L}\{((u,\ell),(v,\ell)):(u,v)\in E(\mathcal G_{\ell,I})\}\cup\{(y,(i,\ell)):i\in\Delta(\mathbf G,\boldsymbol\kappa)\setminus I,\ \ell\in L\})\); thus intervention removes both component edges entering \(I\) and selector edges entering barred copies of \(I\).

definitions.name: \(\mathfrak M_{n,K,d,\tau}\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak M_{n,K,d,\tau}=\{\mathfrak m=(\mathbf G,\boldsymbol\kappa,\mathbf q,\mathbf w):\ \mathcal G_\ell\text{ is a DAG for every }\ell\in L,\ \mathbf w\text{ has positive coordinates summing to one},\ (P_\ell,P_{\ell,I},P_I,\Delta,\mathcal G_{\mathrm m,I})\text{ are the induced objects fixed by the preceding constructions},\ P_I\text{ is simultaneously I-mixture faithful for every }I\subseteq V,\ \max_{t\in V}|\operatorname{pa}_{\cup}(t)|\le d,\ \tau(\mathbf G)\le\tau\}\).

definitions.name: \(\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{tree}}_{n,K}\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{tree}}_{n,K}=\{m\in\mathfrak M_{n,K,n-1,n-2}:\ \operatorname{skel}(\mathcal G_\ell)\text{ is a tree for every }\ell\in[K]\}\).

definitions.name: \(\mathcal O_{\mathbf G}\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal O_{\mathbf G}(I)=\{(A,B,C):A,B,C\subseteq V\text{ are pairwise disjoint and }X_A\perp_{P_I}X_B\mid X_C\}\); by simultaneous I-mixture faithfulness this equals \(\{(A,B,C):\overline A\perp_{d,\mathcal G_{\mathrm m,I}}\overline B\mid\overline C\}\) for every \(I\subseteq V\).

definitions.name: adaptive recovery tree
definitions.construction: A deterministic finite decision tree whose root is labelled by the free answer \(\mathcal O_{\mathbf G}(\varnothing)\), whose internal node after transcript \((I_q,\mathcal O_{\mathbf G}(I_q))_{q<j}\) chooses \(I_j\subseteq V\) with \(|I_j|\le s\), and whose leaf outputs \(\mathsf T(\mathbf G)\).

definitions.name: \(N^{\star}(n,K,d,\tau,s)\)
definitions.construction: \(N^{\star}(n,K,d,\tau,s)=\inf_{\mathcal A}\sup_{\mathfrak m\in\mathfrak M_{n,K,d,\tau}}\operatorname{depth}_{\mathfrak m}(\mathcal A)\), where the infimum ranges over adaptive recovery trees, with value \(\infty\) when no such finite tree recovers \(\mathsf T(\mathbf G)\) for every \(\mathfrak m\).

definitions.name: \(N^{\star}_{\mathrm{tree}}\) and \(N^{\star}_{\mathrm{cf}}\)
definitions.construction: \(N^{\star}_{\mathrm{tree}}(n,K,s)\) and \(N^{\star}_{\mathrm{cf}}(n,K,d,s)\) are obtained from \(\mathrm{def:minimax-count}\) by replacing \(\mathfrak M_{n,K,d,\tau}\) with \(\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{tree}}_{n,K}\) and \(\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{cf}}_{n,K,d}\), respectively.

definitions.name: \(F(n,r,s)\)
definitions.construction: \(F(n,r,s)=\min\{|\mathcal F|:\mathcal F\subseteq\{I\subseteq V:|I|\le s\},\ \forall A\subseteq V\ (|A|=r),\ \forall t\in V\setminus A,\ \exists I\in\mathcal F\text{ with }A\subseteq I\text{ and }t\notin I\}\).

definitions.name: \(U_{\mathrm{PB}}(n,r,s)\)
definitions.construction: \(U_{\mathrm{PB}}(n,r,s)=\begin{cases}\min\left\{\binom nr,\ \min_{r\le k\le s}\left\lceil\frac{\log\!\left(n\binom{n-1}{r}\right)+1}{p_{n,r,k}}\right\rceil\right\},&r\le s<n-1,\\ \min\left\{\binom nr,\ n,\ \min_{r\le k\le n-1}\left\lceil\frac{\log\!\left(n\binom{n-1}{r}\right)+1}{p_{n,r,k}}\right\rceil\right\},&s=n-1.\end{cases}\)

definitions.name: legal blocker-packing handle for \(Q\)
definitions.construction: Map each transcript-compatible true-edge-versus-emergent alternative to its minimal source-plus-last-parent blocker sets; pack alternatives whose distinguishing target families coexist on one legal baseline transcript; choose each next target by maximizing the packed alternatives eliminated per available target slot.

definitions.name: unique-path centroid handle for \(Q_{\mathrm{tree}}\)
definitions.construction: Represent every still-legal tree-mixture alternative by its at most one directed source-to-head path per component; target a componentwise centroid source together with the first surviving child or last-parent blockers and update the potential given by the number of compatible path signatures.

definitions.name: reverse-ancestral packing handle for \(Q_{\mathrm{cf}}\)
definitions.construction: Order candidates by the acyclic relation \(R_{\mathbf G}\) with descendants before ancestors, reuse already certified parents as blockers, and batch compatible heads by a packing of their source-plus-certified-parent target sets.

definitions.name: \(\mathscr D_j\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathscr D_j=\{I\subseteq V:|I|\le s,\ \mathcal O_{\mathfrak g_j}(I)\ne\mathcal O_{\mathfrak g_0}(I)\}\).

statements.justification: This compresses every full conditional-independence answer on the hard subclass to surviving component-descendant sets, making legal transcript lower bounds tractable.
statements.gap: VariciKatzWeiSattigeriTajer2024Interventional uses local marginal descendant tests; it does not state the complete conditional-separation oracle equivalence for arbitrary conditioning sets.
statements.consumer: The lower-bound solver can certify equality of entire adaptive transcripts by comparing descendant signatures instead of enumerating all barred-copy paths.

statements.statement: For every \(\mathfrak m\in\mathfrak M_{n,K,d,0}\), there is a finite exact recovery policy using only targets of size at most \(d\). If \(d=0\), it outputs the empty oriented union without a paid query. If \(d\ge1\), the \(n\) singleton targets recover \(R_{\mathbf G}\) from \(t\in D_{\{a\}}(a)\). For each head \(t\), process its mixture ancestors with strict descendants before strict ancestors, maintain the already certified set \(P_t\subseteq\operatorname{pa}_{\cup}(t)\), and query \(I=P_t\cup\{a\}\) for the next candidate \(a\); declare \(a\in\operatorname{pa}_{\cup}(t)\) exactly when \(t\in D_I(a)\), and stop when \(|P_t|=d\). The policy outputs \(\mathsf T(\mathbf G)\) and uses at most \(n+n(n-1)\) paid queries.
statements.justification: This verifies that the cycle-free endpoint uses the degree budget itself: certified parents block every indirect surviving path before the next source is tested.
statements.gap: VariciKatzWeiSattigeriTajer2024Interventional gives the reverse-ancestor induction but does not formulate the resulting finite minimax recovery policy over the completed shared-kernel model class.
statements.consumer: The feasibility theorem uses this policy to certify that panels of size \(d\), rather than \(d+1\), suffice whenever mixture ancestry is cycle free.

statements.statement: For \(K\ge2\), \(n\ge2\), and \(1\le d\le n-1\), \(N^{\star}(n,K,d,0,s)<\infty\) iff \(s\ge d\); for \(1\le\tau\le n-2\), \(N^{\star}(n,K,d,\tau,s)<\infty\) iff \(s\ge\min\{d+1,n-1\}\). Also \(N^{\star}(n,K,0,\tau,s)=0\). Each necessity direction is witnessed by two legal models with \(\Delta=V\) whose complete oracles agree for every allowed target, and each sufficiency direction recovers \(\mathsf T(\mathbf G)\).
statements.justification: The theorem identifies exactly when bounded interventions contain enough joint blocker capacity for union recovery.
statements.gap: VariciKatzWeiSattigeriTajer2024Interventional proves a local size threshold but does not prove a full-oracle finite-versus-infinite minimax frontier or legal transcript indistinguishability.
statements.consumer: A perturbation platform can rule out an intervention-size budget before collecting data and can identify the smallest multi-target panel size capable of exact latent-state union recovery.

statements.statement: Let \(r=\min\{d+1,n-1\}\). If \(s\ge r\), then \(N^{\star}(n,K,d,\tau,s)\le F(n,r,s)\le U_{\mathrm{PB}}(n,r,s)\). The decoder retains \(a\to t\) exactly when every cover row \(I\) with \(a\in I\) and \(t\notin I\) has \(t\in D_I(a)\); for every nonedge \(a\to t\), the cover contains such a row that also targets an \(r\)-set extending \(\{a\}\cup\operatorname{pa}_{\cup}(t)\).
statements.justification: This is an explicit non-CADIM upper design that exploits last-parent blocking and works without knowing the union skeleton.
statements.gap: CADIM scans ancestor layers with at most quadratic count, while single-DAG separating systems separate endpoints and do not enforce simultaneous parent blockers.
statements.consumer: The bound supplies a concrete bounded-panel schedule whenever the exact adaptive frontier is computationally unavailable.

statements.statement: Let \(\mathfrak g_0,\mathfrak g_1,\ldots,\mathfrak g_m\in\mathfrak M_{n,K,d,\tau}\) have distinct oriented unions, and let \(\mathscr D_j=\{I:|I|\le s,\ \mathcal O_{\mathfrak g_j}(I)\ne\mathcal O_{\mathfrak g_0}(I)\}\). Every exact adaptive recovery tree has depth at least the minimum number of allowed targets whose union hits all \(\mathscr D_j\); in particular, pairwise disjoint nonempty \(\mathscr D_j\) imply depth at least \(m\) along the \(\mathfrak g_0\) transcript.
statements.justification: The lemma isolates the exact legality condition missing from informal transfers of single-DAG separating-system lower bounds.
statements.gap: ShanmugamKocaogluDimakisVishwanath2015SmallInterventions constructs an adaptive total-order transcript for a complete single DAG; it does not ensure simultaneous faithful mixture alternatives.
statements.consumer: Every lower-bound construction in the frontier can be audited by listing one baseline and its full changed-target families.

statements.statement: Every finite graph family used for the feasibility, dense-endpoint, directed-tree, and cycle-free transcript lower bounds admits strictly positive binary component kernels \(\boldsymbol\kappa\), positive mixture weights \(\mathbf w\), and strictly positive shared target laws \(\mathbf q\) such that the induced laws \(P_\ell\), \(P_{\ell,I}\), and \(P_I\) satisfy \(\Delta(\mathbf G,\boldsymbol\kappa)=V\), every declared true edge is active in its child kernel, and simultaneous I-mixture faithfulness holds for every \(I\subseteq V\).
statements.justification: A graphical lower pair is legally relevant to the population oracle only if compatible faithful mechanisms exist for all queried interventions.
statements.gap: The anchor's local necessity examples and the presolve fixtures do not supply an all-parameter simultaneous-faithfulness theorem under padding and topology replication.
statements.consumer: The theorem turns every graphical transcript adversary into a valid population-level impossibility result under the stated bridge.

statements.statement: Using the legal blocker-packing handle, derive an explicit evaluable \(Q(n,K,d,\tau,s)\) and universal constants \(0<c_0\le C_0<\infty\) such that \(c_0Q(n,K,d,\tau,s)\le N^{\star}(n,K,d,\tau,s)\le C_0Q(n,K,d,\tau,s)\) for every feasible \(s\), with the lower inequality certified by legal full-oracle baseline alternatives and the upper inequality attained by an adaptive emergent-path parent-blocking policy.
statements.justification: This is the theorem-level kernel: it replaces a quadratic existence bound by a minimax resource law across every intervention budget.
statements.gap: VariciKatzWeiSattigeriTajer2024Interventional explicitly leaves constrained-size count lower bounds open, and the single-DAG count papers rely on a known skeleton or essential graph.
statements.consumer: The formula determines the number of bounded multi-gene perturbation panels needed to recover a latent cell-state union network at the population-identification level.

statements.statement: Using the unique-path centroid handle, determine the exact closed-form function \(Q_{\mathrm{tree}}(n,K,s)\) such that \(N^{\star}_{\mathrm{tree}}(n,K,s)=Q_{\mathrm{tree}}(n,K,s)\) for every feasible \(s\), and exhibit matching legal directed-tree transcript families.
statements.justification: Unique component paths create a structured regime where exact rather than constant-factor counts should be attainable.
statements.gap: VariciKatzWeiSattigeriTajer2024Interventional gives only the worst-case size of one local tree test, and GreenewaldKatzShanmugamEtAl2019CausalTrees treats one known tree skeleton.
statements.consumer: The formula provides an exact perturbation budget for heterogeneous arborescence models used as sparse regulatory-network approximations.

statements.statement: Using the reverse-ancestral packing handle, determine the exact closed-form function \(Q_{\mathrm{cf}}(n,K,d,s)\) such that \(N^{\star}_{\mathrm{cf}}(n,K,d,s)=Q_{\mathrm{cf}}(n,K,d,s)\) for every \(s\ge d\), and prove matching full-oracle transcript lower bounds within \(\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{cf}}_{n,K,d}\).
statements.justification: Cycle-free mixture ancestry removes the feedback-set penalty while retaining emergent edges, isolating the pure count cost of parent blocking.
statements.gap: The anchor proves optimal maximum intervention size and a headwise quadratic-count algorithm, not an exact adaptive count law.
statements.consumer: The result gives the smallest experiment count for mixtures whose component ancestries admit a common acyclic processing order.

statements.statement: The frontier satisfies the following exact reductions: \(N^{\star}_{\mathrm{cf}}(n,K,1,1)=n\); for two directed trees on three vertices, \(N^{\star}_{\mathrm{tree}}(3,2,1)=\infty\) and \(N^{\star}_{\mathrm{tree}}(3,2,2)=3\); and \(N^{\star}(n,K,n-1,n-2,n-1)=n\).
statements.justification: These exact slices constrain any proposed general formula and expose both adaptive transcript packing and the dense complement-singleton endpoint.
statements.gap: None of the cited mixture papers gives an exact total-intervention count even on these full-oracle subclasses.
statements.consumer: The slices are regression tests for the general frontier and furnish small exact benchmarks for intervention-policy implementations.

sampling_model.design: Adaptive population-oracle design: \(I_j\subseteq V\), \(|I_j|\le s\), is measurable with respect to the preceding complete-oracle transcript; \(I=\varnothing\) is free.
sampling_model.units: On the standard Borel product space \(\mathcal X_V\), component \(\ell\) has DAG \(\mathcal G_\ell\), kernels \(\kappa_{\ell i}\), and law \(P_\ell(dx_V)=\prod_{i\in V}\kappa_{\ell i}(dx_i\mid x_{\operatorname{pa}_\ell(i)})\); the latent component has weights \(\mathbf w\).
sampling_model.treatment: A stochastic hard intervention on \(I\) uses the same kernel \(q_i\) for vertex \(i\) across every component and every target containing \(i\), inducing \(P_{\ell,I}=\prod_{i\in I}q_i\prod_{i\notin I}\kappa_{\ell i}\) and deleting every component and selector edge entering copies of \(I\).
sampling_model.overlap: All mixture weights are strictly positive; no finite-sample conditional-independence margin is imposed.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: None at this stage: \(P_I=\sum_{\ell\in L}w_\ell P_{\ell,I}\), \(\Delta\) is exactly the set of vertices whose lifted observational kernels vary across components, and simultaneous I-mixture faithfulness identifies each complete conditional-independence oracle with barred-copy d-separation in \(\mathcal G_{\mathrm m,I}\).

estimand_functional: \(\bigl(\mathcal O_{\mathbf G}(\varnothing),\mathcal O_{\mathbf G}(I_1),\ldots,\mathcal O_{\mathbf G}(I_N)\bigr)\mapsto\mathsf T(\mathbf G),\quad N=N^{\star}(n,K,d,\tau,s)\)
target_estimand: \(\mathsf T(\mathbf G)=(V,\bigcup_{\ell\in[K]}E(\mathcal G_\ell))\), identified exactly as an oriented union

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The proposed algorithm uses a total of \(\mathcal O(n^2)\) interventions.
For any mixture, an intervention of size at most \(|\operatorname{pa}_{\mathrm m}(i)|+1\) identifies a queried mixture-parent relation.
For some ground-truth ordering, every deterministic adaptive algorithm on a complete skeleton designs a separating system.
A verifying set separates every covered edge that remains unoriented in the observational essential graph.
There is an \(r\)-adaptive single-DAG algorithm with approximation \(\mathcal O(\min\{r,\log n\}n^{1/\min\{r,\log n\}})\) to verification.
With infinite interventional data, the central-node tree algorithm uses at most twice the minimum achievable number of interventions.
Each single-DAG interventional Markov equivalence class has a unique interventional essential-graph representative.
The mixture-DAG representation satisfies a global Markov property for the observational mixture distribution.
Ranks of aggregated moment matrices reveal a shared causal graph when the latent class count is small relative to graph size and sparsity.

tldr: The paper characterizes the experiment-count cost of recovering the oriented union of a latent mixture of DAGs when each intervention can target at most \(s\) variables. The formal kernel is an explicit universal-factor frontier for \(N^{\star}(n,K,d,\tau,s)\), paired with the exact finite-versus-infinite size threshold, legal full-oracle transcript adversaries, and exact count formulas for directed-tree mixtures and cycle-free mixture ancestry. The upper construction batches emergent-path parent blockers; the lower construction packs alternatives that coexist on one I-mixture-faithful baseline transcript.

project_justification.gap: Varıcı et al. identify worst-case local intervention sizes and give a quadratic-count algorithm, but explicitly leave bounded-size intervention-count lower bounds open. Single-DAG count arguments condition on a known skeleton or essential graph and therefore do not control emergent nonedges or selector-induced ancestor cycles.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is a five-parameter minimax resource law for complete I-mixture conditional-independence oracles, including a legal notion of which blocker requirements can coexist against adaptation.
project_justification.fill: The project derives a descendant-signature representation of the hard oracle subclass, proves the exact feasibility boundary, builds an explicit parent-blocking cover, and resolves the remaining gap through a legal blocker-packing benchmark that yields matching universal-factor bounds and exact structured-class formulas.

related_work: Varıcı et al. (2024) supply the component factorization, shared stochastic hard interventions, I-mixture faithfulness, local \(\Delta\)-through-path blocker tests, and CADIM; their Conclusion names constrained-size count lower bounds as open. Shanmugam et al. (2015) show that adaptive discovery on a complete single-DAG skeleton can be forced to realize a separating system, but their total-order transcript does not establish a legal mixture lower pair. Choo, Shiragur, and Bhattacharyya (2022) characterize single-DAG verification by covered-edge separation and compare adaptive search to that benchmark; the present work is informed by their charging idea but replaces covered reversals by true-edge-versus-emergent alternatives. Choo and Shiragur (2023) study round-limited adaptivity for one DAG, not heterogeneous mixture-union identification. Greenewald et al. (2019) motivate a centroid potential for one known causal tree, whereas the tree-mixture result must track \(K\) componentwise paths and a non-tree union. Saeed, Panigrahi, and Uhler (2020) establish observational mixture-DAG Markov semantics under a more restrictive recovery regime. Hauser and Bühlmann (2012) provide the single-DAG equivalence archetype but are not a claimed target of the count theorem. Mazaheri et al. (2026) observe aggregated moment matrices and use their ranks to recover graphical properties of one shared underlying DAG across latent populations. Their observational moment-rank information and shared-graph target are non-nested with the present adaptive interventional-CI oracle and heterogeneous oriented-union target, so their theorem is not a comparator count bound.
technical_internal_limitation: The load-bearing all-parameter step remains coexistence of blocker requirements on one legal baseline transcript. The verified finite evidence is not itself a theorem: exhaustive evaluation covered all \(543\) four-node DAGs paired into \(63{,}432\) union-indegree-at-most-two mixtures and all \(24{,}357{,}888\) barred-copy conditional-separation queries, with no discrepancy from the descendant-signature rule; twelve positive rational fixtures also passed \(6{,}272\) exact probability conditional-independence checks. Uniform faithful realization and the general packing rate remain formal obligations.
honest_scope: The exact feasibility boundary, the size-\(d\) cycle-free policy, full-oracle reduction, explicit parent-blocking upper design, legal transcript lemma, three exact slices, universal-factor frontier, and two structured exact formulas are all posed as results to prove over the completed shared-kernel model. The proposal does not claim finite-sample conditional-independence recovery from faithfulness alone. The classical boundary \(K=1\) is outside the displayed new parameter class and reduces to single-DAG bounded-intervention design; \(d=0\) reduces to the known empty union, and \(s=n-1\) admits the complement-singleton dense reduction.

seed_details.rebuttal: That repetition gives only a quadratic upper bound and no exact minimax count; the mixture union is generally not a tree and its oracle aggregates \(K\) descendant systems.

seed_details.anchor_locations_read: Introduction, Lemma 1, Theorems 1--2 and their proofs, Appendix D.1, and Conclusion.
seed_details.question: Give necessary and sufficient graphical conditions for two \(K\)-DAG mixtures to have identical complete size-\(s\) barred-copy separation oracles, with a canonical partially oriented union representative.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: Uses the structure-identification motif rather than a local do-calculus argument; the deliverable is a global equivalence class and canonical union representative.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace local pairwise separability by a simultaneous equality criterion for every barred-copy separation statement through the latent selector.
seed_details.destination_search: Hauser--Bühlmann and Yang--Katcoff--Uhler characterize single-DAG interventional equivalence, while the mixture papers stop at observational representations or local edge tests.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate by applying ordinary interventional Markov equivalence to the augmented mixture DAG.
seed_details.rebuttal: The augmented object has linked barred copies, a latent selector, an unknown component partition, and a union target; ordinary skeleton and v-structure criteria neither encode the barred-set oracle nor determine invariant union arrows.

seed_details.anchor_locations_read: Introduction, Theorems 1--5, covered-edge induction, graph-separator search proof, and Conclusion.
seed_details.question: Characterize a verification number for a fixed mixture union by hitting minimal true-edge-versus-emergent alternatives.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: Not a relabelled covered-edge number: the primitive alternatives are emergent-nonedge mixture models with unknown union skeletons.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace covered-edge reversals inside a known MEC by full-oracle-equivalent mixture alternatives whose parent blockers may conflict across components.
seed_details.destination_search: No mixture verification benchmark was found; the closest result assumes a known observational essential graph and a single DAG.
seed_details.red_team: A direct relabelling of the covered-edge verification number.
seed_details.rebuttal: Mixture verification must distinguish true edges from emergent nonedges without a known skeleton, so its minimal alternatives are not covered reversals and need not form the covered-edge forest.
seed_details.disposition: not selected because it is better developed after the minimax frontier

seed_details.anchor_locations_read: Introduction, Theorems 1--3, balanced-partition proof, path adversary, and Conclusion.
seed_details.question: Characterize the \(r\)-round size-capped intervention hierarchy for mixture-union recovery.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: Not the cluster-default fully adaptive problem: the additional object is the round-constrained recovery frontier.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace chain-component balanced partitioning by a partition of the version space of legal mixture unions under emergent-path blockers.
seed_details.destination_search: The single-DAG paper leaves even its exact \(r\)-round benchmark open and no I-mixture analogue was found.
seed_details.red_team: The single-DAG \(r n^{1/r}\) argument transfers verbatim.
seed_details.rebuttal: Its proof hides a root in one remaining chordal component, whereas mixture answers can remove several nonlocal alternatives and the union skeleton is not observationally known.
seed_details.disposition: not selected because it introduces an additional round parameter before the fully adaptive benchmark is known

seed_details.anchor_locations_read: Introduction, complete-skeleton separating-system theorem, adaptive adversary proof, randomized lower bound, and Conclusion.
seed_details.question: Determine whether bounded-complexity mixtures admit an exponential gap between optimal adaptive and nonadaptive blocker designs.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The gap must hold on a parameterized family, not a single hand-tuned mixture witness.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace distinct column labels for endpoint separation by labels that encode co-targeting of a source with every surviving last-parent blocker.
seed_details.destination_search: Single-DAG trees exhibit a linear-versus-logarithmic gap, but no mixture result under cyclic-complexity and union-indegree caps was found.
seed_details.red_team: Inherited immediately from the one-tree lower and upper bounds.
seed_details.rebuttal: A mixture of directed trees need not have a tree union, and a query reveals the union of several descendant systems, so both the nonadaptive lower code and adaptive centroid progress require new arguments.
seed_details.disposition: not selected because the direction depends on the unresolved full-adaptivity frontier

seed_details.anchor_locations_read: Introduction, generalized cost objective, Theorems 4--5, verification construction, and Conclusion.
seed_details.question: Optimize a mixture blocker policy under heterogeneous node costs and a per-query cardinality cap, with a certifying lower benchmark.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: A weighted set-cover formulation alone is insufficient; an optimality certificate against legal transcript alternatives is required.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the covered-edge forest vertex cover by a weighted hitting problem over mixture parent-blocker certificates.
seed_details.destination_search: Cost-optimal designs exist for single-DAG skeletons, but no cost certificate for I-mixture union recovery was found.
seed_details.rebuttal: The nontrivial question is to prove that the hit alternatives coexist on a legal full-oracle transcript and that the adaptive design is certified against that same benchmark, not merely to solve a supplied set cover.
seed_details.disposition: not selected because it is a downstream objective change

seed_details.anchor_locations_read: Introduction, finite-sample experiments, Theorems 3--4, and Conclusion.
seed_details.question: Convert a separating intervention policy into a fixed-confidence sequential recovery rule whose sample complexity is instance-adaptive to mixture-oracle margins.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: M8 is only the finite-sample rung; the underlying object remains exact structural recovery.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace exact conditional-independence answers by anytime-valid tests indexed by the adaptively selected conditioning triples.
seed_details.destination_search: Adaptive finite-sample single-DAG allocation results do not address latent mixture selectors or emergent-path CI margins.
seed_details.red_team: Standard confidence sequences can be wrapped around CADIM.
seed_details.rebuttal: Faithfulness supplies no quantitative margin, and adaptive reuse of samples across exponentially many conditioning statements makes both stopping validity and optimal allocation new; the required margin model is outside the present oracle kernel.
seed_details.disposition: not selected because it requires an additional separation-margin model

seed_details.question: Characterize the count reduction when a subset of mechanism-varying nodes or component ancestral relations is known before experimentation.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The side information must yield an iff count frontier, not a qualitative monotonicity statement.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Restrict the parent-blocker family using the known domain map and derive a necessity witness respecting that information.
seed_details.destination_search: The anchor notes partial domain knowledge as future work but gives no count theorem; multi-context papers assume observed domain labels instead.
seed_details.red_team: Monotonicity under side information makes the result immediate.
seed_details.rebuttal: Monotonicity gives no exact threshold or count; the hard part is an information-respecting legal transcript pair and a matching compressed blocker design.
seed_details.disposition: not selected because it narrows the model before the no-side-information frontier is understood

threads: Varıcı et al. (2024), Theorems 1--4 and Conclusion: exact local size thresholds, cycle-sensitive CADIM, and an explicit open constrained-count lower-bound problem.

Shanmugam et al. (2015), complete-skeleton theorem and adaptive adversary: bounded-size separating systems remain necessary on a single-DAG clique, but the adversary chooses a total order rather than a legal mixture transcript.
Choo, Shiragur, and Bhattacharyya (2022), Theorems 1--5: verification is covered-edge separation and search is logarithmically competitive, conditional on a known single-DAG essential graph.

Mazaheri et al. (2026): ranks of aggregated observational moment matrices reveal graphical properties of one shared underlying DAG across latent populations, an information model and target distinct from adaptive interventional-CI recovery of a heterogeneous union.
literature_map.occupancy: No paper found gives a minimax intervention-count frontier for recovering the oriented union of heterogeneous component DAGs under complete I-mixture conditional-independence oracles.
literature_map.method_adapted: The lower side adapts the adaptive separating-system transcript adversary; the upper side adapts covered-alternative charging but replaces edge separation by emergent-path parent blocking.
literature_map.no_subsuming_paper: The 2026 mixture neighbor uses observational moment-matrix ranks to study one shared underlying DAG, so it does not subsume the adaptive interventional-CI count problem for a union of heterogeneous component DAGs.

threads: Varıcı et al. (2024), Theorem 2 proof: one componentwise child blocker per directed-tree path yields a local \(K+1\) size bound.
Varıcı et al. (2024), Theorem 3 proof: reverse ancestor layers permit sequential parent blocking in the cycle-free case, but still scan candidates head by head.
Greenewald et al. (2019): a central-node policy is within factor two for one known undirected causal tree and information-greedy policies may be exponentially worse.
Kocaoglu, Dimakis, and Vishwanath (2017): limited-intervention design is tractable on known single-DAG tree and clique-tree skeletons.
literature_map.occupancy: No exact total-count formula was found for arbitrary directed-tree mixtures or for the cycle-free mixture-ancestor class.
literature_map.method_adapted: The proposed handles combine unique component paths or reverse ancestral order with a potential over still-legal mixture-union alternatives.
literature_map.no_subsuming_paper: The tree exemplars assume a single known skeleton and cannot represent emergent pairs or cross-component ancestor cycles.

threads: Hauser and Bühlmann (2012): an if-and-only-if criterion and unique essential graph for single-DAG perfect-intervention equivalence.
Yang, Katcoff, and Uhler (2018): an augmented intervention-DAG criterion for general single-DAG interventions.
Saeed, Panigrahi, and Uhler (2020): the observational mixture DAG has a global Markov semantics and supports union recovery under poset compatibility.
Varıcı et al. (2024), Appendix D.1: distinct component partitions can remain indistinguishable, but no global size-capped equivalence criterion is supplied.
literature_map.occupancy: No canonical size-capped interventional equivalence object for heterogeneous DAG mixtures was found.
literature_map.method_adapted: The prospective proof adapts augmented-graph equivalence and essential-graph uniqueness to barred copies linked by a latent selector.
literature_map.no_subsuming_paper: Existing mixture representations address observational Markov structure or local interventional separability, not equality of every complete barred-copy oracle answer.
